findings.issue: clearCartBestEffort never threw. remote.clearCart now runs enqueueClearCart outside any try, so a DB error on the outbox insert propagates. For CARD and COD that means a 500 for an order that already exists with its payment created. For COD it also skips the events.publish(placedType, saved) on line 425, so ORDER_PLACED is never recorded. On the 409 path (line 284) the same error turns the intended RESOURCE_CONFLICT into a 500. The chance is low, since the same DB backs the event outbox, but this failure mode is new.
findings.fix: For COD, publish the placed event before the clear. Or make clearCart catch and log an enqueue failure as WARN (the fingerprint guard still blocks a re-order, as the design's residual-risk note says). Keep the WALLET enqueue inside the markPaid transaction as it is.

findings.issue: clearCarriesOnlyTheConsumedLines changes the cart mock (cartHolds(later, 1)) only after place() has returned, and the inline clear has already run by then. The never()-includes-later check therefore passes even if the implementation re-read the cart at clear time, so this test does not prove AC-18 on the order side. AC-18 is still proven where it matters, by the cart-side tests: CartConsumedLinesIntegrationTest changedQuantitySurvives and laterLineSurvives, and InternalCartControllerTest laterLinesSurvive. The relay path can only use the stored payload.
findings.fix: Make carts.getCart() return the consumed cart on the first call and the cart with the later line on any further call. Or assert on the stored CLEAR_CART payload with the cart service down, then deliver it through the relay after cartHolds(later).

findings.issue: All clears for one user share the aggregate cart:<userId>. A CLEAR_CART row that can never succeed, such as a 4xx from validation drift, is retried for about 26 h, and the relay holds back every later clear for that user for that whole time. Inline attempts still clear new orders, so only relay retries of that user's later clears are delayed. An order's own events are never blocked: they use the order-id aggregate, and a name-based UUID cannot collide with a random v4 id.
findings.fix: Optional: treat a FeignException 4xx other than 404/408/429 on CLEAR_CART as DEAD right away, or document the head-of-line effect in the runbook.

findings.issue: complete() only moves PENDING rows to DONE. If the 409 path's inline retry succeeds for an order whose clear is already DEAD (for example after rollback step 2), the row stays DEAD and stays on the admin list even though the cart was cleared.
findings.fix: Optionally include status 'DEAD' in complete(), or note in the runbook that such rows can be ignored or retried harmlessly.

findings.issue: walletCartOrderEnqueuesThenAttempts checks call order on a mocked OrderRemote. It does not check that the enqueue joins the markPaid transaction: moving the enqueue after tx.execute but before the attempt would still pass. No test covers WALLET buy-now (the code is clearly guarded).
findings.fix: Optionally add a test that makes markPaid or events.publish throw inside the transaction and asserts that no CLEAR_CART row exists.

findings.issue: The AC-15 bound check (next_attempt_at - now() <= 240) always passes: an inline failure leaves next_attempt_at at its insert default of now(). The real cap is proven separately in OutboxRelayTest.clearCartBackoffIsCappedPerKind.
findings.fix: Change the message to 'due immediately' or assert <= 0.

findings.issue: removeConsumed calls lockOrCreateCart, so a consumed call for a user with no cart (or with empty lines) creates an empty cart row. This is harmless and the endpoint is internal and token-guarded.
findings.fix: Optionally return 0 early for empty lines, or use a lock-if-exists query.

summary: I approve PR-C at 71bba97 with three minor findings and four nits; none blocks the merge. The change matches design part C and CTO conditions 1 to 3. CLEAR_CART uses the existing outbox. The aggregate is per user (cart:<userId>), so it never blocks an order's own events, and the idem key is CLEAR_CART:<orderId>. In fail(), CLEAR_CART rows cap their backoff at 240 s and go DEAD at 400 attempts; other kinds keep 3600 s and 20. PR-A's unknown-kind tolerance still holds: KNOWN is built from Kind.values(), and the BOGUS tests are unchanged. place() is not transactional. For WALLET orders the enqueue joins the tx.execute markPaid/ORDER_PLACED transaction, and the network call runs after the commit; CARD and COD enqueue and then attempt with no transaction open. deleteConsumed is scoped to the user's cart under the cart row lock. It matches product, variant_key, offer_key and quantity exactly, and compares added_at with date_trunc to the millisecond. A changed or later line survives, and a repeat deletes 0. The internal endpoint takes a UUID path and @Valid, with lines capped at 50 and quantity 1 to 99. orderId is never used for scoping. The existing TokenFilter returns 401 for no, wrong and unconfigured tokens, and all three are tested. The gateway test internalPathsAreNotRouted shows a 404 with nothing proxied, with a positive control. Buy-now never reads or clears the cart. The runbook and ADR 0010 have the ordered rollback steps, the PR-A-first deploy order and the DEAD retry. The C0 follow-ups from review B are resolved: the javadoc and test name are fixed, a variant-and-offer parity test pins the availableQuantity difference, and AC-10 now has verifyNoMoreInteractions plus variant, offer and seller checks; the optional helper nit was not taken. Most tests would catch their regression: idempotency, the scoping SQL including cart_id and date_trunc, the per-kind cap and attempt limit, WALLET enqueue, the 409 re-clear and the token checks. The weak ones are the order-side AC-18 test, the trivially true AC-15 bound check and a WALLET test that only checks call order. I did not re-check the quoted mutation failures: the work folder has no evidence.md, and log.md does not record them. Verify passed per verify-C.md. The minors worth fixing: an outbox enqueue failure now propagates (a 500 on a placed order, and a COD placed event that can be skipped), the order-side AC-18 test cannot fail, and one permanently failing clear holds back that user's later relay clears for about 26 h.
